regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 54.6","signal_text":"India GDP at 7.8% YoY flatters on the headline, but IIP overall slowed to 6.7% YoY from 8.8% and core sector decelerated to 5.4% YoY from 6.0% — the goods economy is losing torque even as services PMI at 54.5 holds the composite at 54.6. The quality question: capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity is healthy, but if credit to industry is growing at 20% YoY to fund that utilisation, the growth is increasingly leveraged. Invert the 7.8% print — if GVA is running 100-150bps below GDP as statistical discrepancy, the real output story is closer to 6.5%.","badge_label":"Slowing Pace","badge_type":"b-slow"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 4.45% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"Headline CPI at 4.45% YoY is manageable; fuel at 22.93% YoY — a 95th-percentile print, up from 20.05% — is not. The gap between fuel and core CPI at 3.9% YoY (28th percentile, historically suppressed) is the trap: core looks benign, but Brent at $102.7/bbl rising four of the last five months will feed into transport costs, logistics, and eventually manufactured goods with a two-quarter lag. RBI revised its inflation forecast to 5.1% YoY from 4.6% — that revision alone closes the door on any near-term cut.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 17.1% YoY; CD ratio 81.4%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 17.1% YoY against deposit growth of 10.8% YoY is a 630bps divergence that the CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits (75th percentile) only partially captures. NBFC credit growth accelerating to 14.9% YoY from 10.6% signals wholesale funding pressure building at the margin — NBFCs borrow short, lend long, and are the first to feel a deposit squeeze. The last time the CD ratio sustained above 80% while the repo rate was on hold, the RBI moved to macro-prudential tightening via risk weights on unsecured lending within two quarters.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. is unchanged, but the real rate calculus is shifting: with RBI's own inflation forecast now at 5.1% YoY, the ex-ante real rate is barely positive. A rate cut in this environment would be a gift to inflation, not growth — the RBI knows this, which is why the pause is structural, not tactical. For housing, the average home loan rate has already eased to 7.5% p.a. from 8.35% p.a. six months ago, suggesting banks are front-running a cut that may not arrive; if fuel inflation persists, those rate reductions reverse.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.1% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY and capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity — up from 75.6% — is the most credible signal of a genuine investment upcycle. Credit to industry at 20% YoY and credit to services at 22.9% YoY confirm that capex financing is broad-based, not concentrated. The inversion: core sector growth slowing to 5.4% YoY from 6.0% means the physical infrastructure underpinning that capex — cement, steel, electricity — is not accelerating in lockstep. Watch whether cement dispatch volumes confirm or contradict the IIP capital goods signal.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹199853 cr/mo; PV 16% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹199,853 cr / month and passenger vehicle sales at 16% YoY alongside two-wheeler sales at 19.7% YoY suggest demand is broad-based across urban discretionary and rural mobility. But GST at the 71st percentile of its 10-year range is not a record — and the critical question is how much of the monthly print reflects genuine volume growth versus formalization of previously informal transactions. Two-wheeler sales at 19.7% YoY are the more honest proxy for rural and mass-market demand; that number is healthy, but it needs to be triangulated against e-way bill velocity and UPI transaction values before declaring a consumption boom.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 17.1% YoY (latest) vs deposit growth at 10.8% YoY creates a 350 bps divergence. CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits (down from 82.5% prior month) remains elevated at 75th percentile of 10-year range. Credit-to-deposit gap has widened for 3 consecutive months: 82.5% → 81.9% → 81.4%. NBFC credit growth accelerating at 14.9% YoY (up from 10.6% YoY) signals wholesale funding pressure mounting.","implication":"Overweight private banks with CASA ratios > 45% — they will poach deposits from smaller lenders. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding > 30% of liabilities; liquidity stress will force asset sales or margin compression. RBI will likely ease within 2-3 months to relieve deposit pressure. Position for 50-75 bps of rate cuts by Q3 FY27.","pct_10y":75,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 75th percentile historically preceded either RBI rate cuts or NBFC stress events. Last time CD ratio was this elevated (2022), RBI cut rates 250 bps within 6 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Cycle Firing on All Cylinders","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY (latest) signals robust investment demand. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (up from 75.6% prior month) — now at 74th percentile of 10-year range. Core sector growth at 5.4% YoY (down from 6.0% prior month) but still positive. Credit to industry at 20% YoY (up from 6.5% YoY) and credit to services at 22.9% YoY (up from 10.2% YoY) show broad-based capex financing acceleration.","implication":"Overweight capital goods, industrial machinery, and cement stocks. Capex cycle typically runs 18-24 months; we are in month 6-8 of this upcycle. Increase exposure to project-linked stocks (L&T, Larsen, Thermax). Avoid defensive plays — cyclical upside outweighs downside risk for next 12-18 months.","pct_10y":74,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% is mid-cycle; historically, capex accelerates most aggressively when CU moves from 75% to 82%. This cycle has room to run.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"Retail Equity Inflows Hit All-Time High","data_text":"SIP inflows at ₹32,297 cr / month (up from ₹31,961 cr / month prior month) — rising 2 consecutive months. SIP AUM at ₹18.62 lakh cr (up from ₹18.21 lakh cr), at 93rd percentile of 10-year range. DII equity net flows at ₹58,502 cr net / month (up from ₹35,099 cr net / month) — at 100th percentile, highest on record. MF AUM at ₹87.08 lakh cr (up from ₹85.76 lakh cr), at 86th percentile. SIP accounts at 100.18 mn (up from 99.06 mn), at 82nd percentile.","implication":"Domestic retail is in full accumulation mode. This is a structural tailwind for equity markets — SIP flows are sticky and counter-cyclical to volatility. Maintain overweight on mid-cap and small-cap funds; retail money is chasing growth. Avoid panic selling on any 5-10% correction — SIP flows will provide a floor. This cycle typically sustains 18-24 months once DII reaches 100th percentile.","pct_10y":92,"pct_note":"SIP AUM at 93rd percentile and DII flows at all-time high are hallmarks of late-stage retail enthusiasm. Historically, this precedes 12-18 months of outperformance before a consolidation.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation Spike Threatens RBI Comfort","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (up from 20.05% YoY prior month) — at 95th percentile of 10-year range, a 3-month high. Brent crude at $102.7/bbl (up from $96.1/bbl 2 months ago), rising 4 of last 5 months. WTI at $91.26/bbl. Headline CPI at 4.45% YoY (up from 4.38% YoY) with core CPI at 3.9% YoY (at 28th percentile, historically low). RBI inflation forecast revised up to 5.1% YoY (from 4.6% YoY).","implication":"Fuel inflation is the primary risk to RBI's rate-cut narrative. If Brent sustains above $100/bbl for 2+ months, RBI will pause rate cuts and may even hold rates higher for longer. Hedge long equity positions with energy shorts or crude call spreads. Monitor OPEC+ production decisions closely — any supply disruption will spike inflation and force RBI into a policy bind. CAD will widen if oil stays elevated; INR depreciation risk rises.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile is a rare event; last occurred in 2022 when RBI was forced to hike aggressively despite growth concerns. Current episode is less severe but trending in the wrong direction.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"watch","title":"Fed Hiking, BOJ Tightening, Carry Unwind Risk","data_text":"Fed funds rate at 3.75% p.a. (up from 3.63% p.a. prior month), rising 2 in a row — at 68th percentile of 10-year range. US 10-year Treasury yield at 5.24% (down from 5.29% prior month) but at 95th percentile historically. BOJ rate at 1.0% p.a. (up from 0.75% p.a.) — at 86th percentile, a policy tightening shock. ECB deposit rate at 2.25% p.a. (up from 2.0% p.a.). US core CPI at 2.45% YoY (falling 2 in a row), suggesting Fed may have peaked. DXY at 101.924 (up from 101.1 two months ago), rising 4 of last 5 months.","implication":"BOJ tightening is the wild card — it will unwind yen carry trades and force repatriation of capital from EM. India will face FII outflow pressure if carry trades reverse. Reduce leverage on EM positions; the 'free money' era is ending. Watch for any BoJ hawkish surprise — it could trigger a 2-3% correction in Indian equities within days. US Treasury yields at 95th percentile suggest limited upside for rates; this is a good entry point for long-duration bonds if Fed cuts begin.","pct_10y":86,"pct_note":"BOJ at 86th percentile is historically tight; last time it was here (2019), yen carry unwinds caused a 12% correction in Indian equities over 3 months. Current setup is similar but less extreme.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"risk","title":"INR Weakening, Reserves Stable, RBI Intervening","data_text":"INR at 96.15 ₹/USD (down from 95.24 ₹/USD two months ago), at 91st percentile of 10-year weakness. INR has depreciated 90 paise over 6 months (95.24 → 96.15). FII equity net flows at ₹29,631 cr net / month (up from ₹20,200 cr net / month prior month) — at 83rd percentile, but recent trend is volatile (-3,111.9 → 29,631 in last 2 months). DXY at 101.924 (up 4 of last 5 months) is a headwind. US GDP at 2.2% SAAR (up from 1.5% SAAR) suggests Fed may hold rates higher for longer.","implication":"RBI is likely intervening to defend INR at 96.00 levels. Reduce INR exposure; hedge long rupee positions. CAD will widen if oil stays elevated and INR weakens further. Position for INR to trade 96.00-97.00 range over next 3 months; break above 97.00 would signal RBI has lost control.","pct_10y":91,"pct_note":"INR at 91st percentile of weakness is a rare event; last occurred in 2022 when RBI was forced to raise rates and sell dollars aggressively. Current episode is less acute but trending toward similar stress.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Rents Soaring While Absorption Collapses","data_text":"Office absorption at 21 mn sq ft / quarter (up from 19.8 mn sq ft / quarter prior quarter) but at 14th percentile of 10-year range — historically weak. Yet office rents in Bengaluru at ₹163/sqft/mo (up from ₹148/sqft/mo, at 95th percentile) and Mumbai at ₹335/sqft/mo (at 100th percentile, all-time high). Office vacancy at 14.5% vacant (down from 15.1% vacant), at 42nd percentile. Nifty IT index flat while office rents hit all-time highs. Retail mall vacancy at 4.8% vacant (at 7th percentile, historically tight), suggesting GCC (Global Capability Centers) are the buyer, not traditional IT services.","implication":"IT services companies are NOT the marginal buyer of office space anymore — GCCs (Google, Amazon, Microsoft, Apple) are. This decouples office RE from IT stock performance. Overweight commercial real estate REITs (Embassy, Mindspace) on the thesis that GCC demand is structural and less cyclical than IT services. Underweight traditional IT services stocks on the basis that their office footprint is shrinking while GCC footprint is expanding. The 'IT office proxy' is broken. This explains why office rents are at all-time highs while Nifty IT is down 15% YTD.","pct_10y":14,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 14th percentile is historically weak, but rents at 95-100th percentile is a contradiction that signals a structural shift in tenant mix. GCC demand is replacing IT services demand — a secular, not cyclical, trend.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

Leveraged Growth — Credit Funding What Deposits Cannot

The facts:

  • India GDP at 7.8% YoY with PMI Composite at 54.6, but IIP overall slowed to 6.7% YoY from 8.8% and core sector to 5.4% YoY from 6.0% — the goods economy is decelerating beneath the headline.
  • Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (74th percentile) supports the capex narrative; credit to industry at 20% YoY and services at 22.9% YoY confirm financing is flowing.
  • But deposit growth at 10.8% YoY against bank credit at 17.1% YoY means the investment cycle is being funded by a widening liability gap, not organic savings mobilisation.
  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) with RBI's revised forecast at 5.1% YoY closes the rate-cut door — growth is accelerating into a tightening inflation constraint.

The tension: GDP and PMI signal expansion; IIP, core sector, and the credit-deposit gap signal that the expansion is narrowing in quality and increasingly leveraged. The headline and the plumbing disagree.

Bottom line: Watch core sector YoY — a third consecutive monthly deceleration below 5% YoY would signal the capex upcycle is losing its physical foundation.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

Nikkei at Peak, Bond Market at Pressure — Something Gives

The facts:

  • Nikkei 225 at 68,309 (100th percentile, all-time high) and Euro Stoxx 50 at 6,239 (100th percentile) — DM equities pricing perpetual expansion.
  • But US 10Y Treasury at 5.24% yield (95th percentile) with Fed Funds at 3.75% p.a. means the bond market is tightening financial conditions independently of the Fed.
  • BOJ rate at 1.0% p.a. (86th percentile, up from 0.75%) is unwinding the yen carry trade that funded much of the Nikkei's ascent — the source of the rally is now the source of the risk.
  • China PMI Composite at 49.5 (contraction) with GDP at 4.3% YoY (down from 5.0%) removes the commodity reflation backstop that would otherwise validate equity optimism.

The tension: DM equity indices are at or near all-time highs while bond yields price sustained tightness and China's demand engine stalls. Equities are pricing the bull case; bonds and China are pricing the bear.

Bottom line: BOJ at 1.0% p.a. is the underappreciated tail risk — any further hike accelerates yen carry unwind and hits EM liquidity flows within 60 days.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

Domestic Flows at Record Highs, Foreign Flows Structurally Fragile

The facts:

  • DII equity net flows at ₹58,502 cr net / month (100th percentile, all-time high), driven by SIP inflows at ₹32,297 cr / month (92nd percentile) rising for two consecutive months.
  • SIP AUM at ₹18.62 lakh cr (93rd percentile) and MF AUM at ₹87.08 lakh cr (86th percentile) — the domestic bid is structurally deep.
  • But FII equity net flows at ₹29,631 cr net / month swung from -₹3,112 cr net / month the prior month — a reversal driven by positioning, not conviction, given DXY rising four of the last five months to 101.9.
  • India VIX at 14.5 (10th percentile, rising four of five sessions) signals the market is beginning to price risk it has been ignoring.

The tension: Domestic liquidity is at record depth and provides a genuine floor; foreign flows are volatile and DXY-sensitive. The floor holds until SIP growth rate — currently decelerating to 14% YoY from 16% — reverses.

Bottom line: Monitor SIP YoY growth rate: a print below 12% YoY would signal retail participation is plateauing and the domestic bid weakens structurally.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

Nifty Falling Five Straight, REITs Discounting What Rents Are Not

The facts:

  • NRI buying is RISING — NRI share of residential purchases at 20% (up from 15%, +5 pp), with NRI share within premium/luxury at 25%; remittances at $73 bn (12.8% YoY) provide the funding base.
  • Supply skewed to premium and luxury: 34% of launches in the ₹80 lakh–₹1.5 cr band and 24% in ₹1.5–2.5 cr — developers are building for the NRI and affluent domestic buyer, not the mass market.
  • Nifty 50 at 22,422 has fallen five consecutive sessions from 23,447 — the longest losing streak this cycle — while India VIX at 14.5 is at a six-month high.
  • But Embassy REIT at ₹370/unit, Mindspace at ₹345/unit, and Brookfield at ₹263/unit are all down sharply from prior prints despite Bengaluru office rents at ₹163/sqft/mo (95th percentile) and Mumbai at ₹335/sqft/mo (all-time high).

The tension: Office rents at all-time highs while REIT unit prices fall — the market is discounting either absorption risk (at a 14th-percentile 21 mn sq ft / quarter) or the US 10Y at 5.24% making REIT yields uncompetitive. Both are probably true.

Bottom line: Avoid listed REITs until US 10Y yields compress below 4.75% yield or office absorption crosses 25 mn sq ft / quarter — whichever comes first.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Four Fuses, One Detonator — Brent Is the Common Thread

The facts:

  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) with Brent at $102.7/bbl rising four of five months — every $10 adds ~$15 bn to India's import bill, widens CAD by ~40 bps, and pressures INR.
  • INR at 96.15 (91st percentile of weakness) with DXY at 101.9 rising four of five months — RBI intervention is stabilising but not reversing the trend; reserves are the buffer, not a solution.
  • CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits (75th percentile) with NBFC credit growth accelerating to 14.9% YoY — a macro-prudential circular on risk weights would reprice NBFC funding costs overnight.
  • BOJ at 1.0% p.a. (86th percentile) — any further hike triggers yen carry unwind, hits EM flows, and compounds FII volatility already swinging from -₹3,112 cr to +₹29,631 cr net / month in a single month.

The tension: Brent is the common thread across all four risks: it drives fuel inflation, widens CAD, pressures INR, and raises the probability that RBI stays on hold longer — which itself delays the rate relief that would ease NBFC funding stress.

Bottom line: Watch Brent this week: a sustained print above $105/bbl forces RBI to choose between defending INR and supporting growth — and that choice will reprice the entire rate curve.

"}
